:::{#cor-vcov-indpt-diagonal}
#### Independent components give a diagonal variance matrix

Let $\vX = \tp{(X_1, \ldots, X_p)}$ be a random vector
whose components are each discrete or continuous,
with:

- $\E{X_i^2} < \infty$ for every $i$, and
- $X_i$ and $X_j$ [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt) for every $i \neq j$.

Then $\Varf{\vX}$ is
[diagonal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-diagonal-matrix),
with diagonal elements $\Var{X_1}, \ldots, \Var{X_p}$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-vcov-elements, the $(i,j)$-th element of $\Varf{\vX}$ is $\Covs{X_i}{X_j}$.
For $i \neq j$, $X_i$ and $X_j$ are independent,
so $\Covs{X_i}{X_j} = 0$ by @thm-indpt-uncorrelated.
The $(i,i)$-th element is $\Covs{X_i}{X_i} = \Var{X_i}$ by @lem-cov-xx.

:::
